main_text.p: I. A ualis vel pitualis.ctualis, & habitualis. Actualis est assensus conclusionis: Habitualis verò, habitus per eam generatus. De utraq; potest cognitio hoc in loco sumi. In communi autem modo loquendi, pro habituali potius sumitur. Reliquae verò particulae ponuntur loco differentiae, ut per eas distinguatur a reliquis habitibus intellectus.entia Nam Vera dicitur cognitio, ut distinguatur ab errore: Certa, ut distinguatur ab opinione, & cæteris habitibus contingenter veris, quibus non repugnat subesse falsum.modo Per Rem necessariam, separatur a Prudentia & Arte, quæ versantur circa contingentia. Particula denique per cau-sam, distinguit scientiam ab habitu principiorum,erat qui non procedit per medium, sed immediatè assentitur veritati, habita notitia terminorum. Per eandem particulam distinguitur a scientia, quæ habetur a posteriori, per effectum. Eam enim hoc loco non intelligit Aristoteles, sed tantùm scientiam perfectam, quam vocant a priori, & propter quid.b De hac definitione movent interpretes quæstionem, an sit completa, vel desit ei particula, evidens, saltem subintelligenda? Hæc quæstio ut enodetur, explicandi sunt tres illi termini, Certitudo, Necessitas, Evidentia. Rubius 2. tract. de habit. q. 1. Itaq;

titudo d iit?Certitudo, est firma adhæsio intellectus alicui objecto absq; dubitatione, vel formidine: ut illam definiunt Dd. Scholastici, in 3. d. q. 26. Thom. q. 2. art. 4. Bonavent. q. 4. Durand. in 4. dist. 37. q. 8. Cæterum firma ista intellectus adhæsio duplex est; apparens & vera. Apparens est, quando intellectus, ex aliquâ ratione probabili, atq; ex efficaci applicatione voluntatis, tenaciter inhæret alicui ob-titudo lex pparens.jecto:

page.notes: Only the left edge of the page is visible, so most words are cut off after a few letters and cannot be completed. The bold-looking words Erro, Opi, Pru and Art are set apart, and may be a list. Several letters at the cut are uncertain and are not marked, because the cut hides them. The line "tiâ," shows a macron-like mark over the a, which I read as â. Marginal fragments at the left edge (ore, inione, dentia, c, &, elligen-, & entia à, teriori.) and the notes at the top left are cut and only partly legible; their placement against the text lines is approximate. The reading of the note "titudo lex pparens." is uncertain, and the note "ualis vel pitualis." reads "yel" for "vel" in the scan. Italic and roman boundaries in the body are estimated from the scan.
